steps: Make an 'I love you' handshape with your dominant hand, extending your thumb, index finger, and pinkie.
Hold the hand in the space in front of your shoulder at about chest height.
Glide the hand forward twice in short, even movements, as if a plane were cruising onward.
Keep your palm facing the floor through the entire movement.
Look in the direction your hand travels with a relaxed, neutral expression.
tip: This is the same production as AIRPLANE — context tells them apart: DRIVE-to AIRPORT versus GET-in AIRPLANE.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you, palm facing up, as your canvas.
Make an 'I' handshape with your dominant hand, extending only your pinkie finger.
Touch the pad of your pinkie to the flat palm and draw a few short strokes, as if sketching with a pencil.
Then add the person marker: hold both flat hands out at your sides with fingers pointing outward.
Sweep both flat hands straight down along your torso, keeping the palms facing each other.
Finish the movement with a slight nod, as if presenting the finished artist.
tip: ART is Lifeprint's DRAW sign done with a pinkie brush — adding the flat-hands-down person ending turns an action into its doer, the same pattern as TEACHER.

steps: Make an 'F' handshape with your dominant hand, touching your thumb to your index finger and spreading the other three fingers.
Hold the hand out at chest height with the palm facing forward.
Wave the hand from side to side a couple of times using small, tight movements.
Keep the path strictly side to side and never let the hand circle.
Keep a neutral, matter-of-fact expression while signing.
tip: Side-to-side is FURNITURE; drawing a circle with the same 'F' hand means FRIDAY — the classic beginner mix-up.

steps: Form an 'F' handshape with each hand, touching each thumb to its index finger and spreading the other fingers.
Hold both hands in front of your chest with the palms facing down toward the floor.
Start with the hands close together near the center of your chest.
Move both hands away from each other in opposite directions in one smooth, even motion.
Keep your palms facing down and your elbows relaxed through the whole movement.
Hold a calm, neutral expression as you finish.
tip: Picture unrolling a diploma scroll: the 'F' hands show its width and the outward movement its length. For temperature or extent, Lifeprint points to a different DEGREE sign.

steps: Make an 'F' handshape with your dominant hand, touching your thumb to your index finger and spreading the other fingers.
Touch the 'F' hand against your chest or torso where a shirt button would sit.
Arc the hand downward a few inches along your torso.
Touch your torso again to mark the position of a second button.
Repeat once more to show a third button if you want to show several.
Keep a neutral expression and let the taps mark each button's place.
tip: Two or three taps is plenty — the round 'F' handshape already shows the button's shape, so you never need to tap every button on the shirt.

steps: Raise your dominant hand to your forehead with your thumb and fingertips loosely gathered.
Pinch the thumb and fingertips together as if grasping the brim of an imaginary baseball cap.
Give the imaginary brim a small tug forward and slightly downward.
Keep your palm facing down as you tip the cap.
Finish with a relaxed, neutral expression.
tip: Forehead placement marks the masculine set (boy, dad, brother) — a tipped cap from the era when men wore hats; the feminine set is placed at the chin instead.

steps: Make an 'I' handshape with your dominant hand, forming a fist with only the pinkie extended.
Touch the tip of your pinkie against the middle of your forehead.
Flick the pinkie away from your forehead with a small upward jerk.
Shift your hand slightly to one side and repeat the forehead touch and flick once more.
Keep your palm facing outward as the pinkie pops off the forehead.
Raise your eyebrows slightly, as if a bright thought has just struck.
tip: One flick is IDEA; repeating it with a small sideways shift applies ASL's plural sweep — the same doubling that turns CHILD into CHILDREN.
